newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland's Kolodko asks auditors for AgMin probe.
newsitem.headline: Poland's Kolodko asks auditors for AgMin probe.

text.p: Polish Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko on Wednesday asked the Supreme Auditing Chamber (NIK) to probe the Agriculture Ministry's activities surrounding grain imports, the finance ministry's press office said.
Kolodko asked for an investigation of the Agriculture Ministry-linked food market regulator, the Farm Market Agency (ARR) and intermediary firms involved in grain trade.
"Minister Kolodko asked NIK to investigate the (Farm Market) Agency," a press office official told Reuters.

The official also said Kolodko asked NIK to investigate the activities of Agriculture Minister Roman Jagielinski, who on Tuesday pushed through the cabinet a regulation reintroducing duties on grain imports, which had been set to stay free of duty until mid-1997.
PAP news agency quoted Kolodko as saying the Agriculture Ministry had an obligation to stabilise food prices and care for the interests not only of producers but also consumers.
Kolodko, who was the only cabinet member to oppose reintroduction of the duties, said on Tuesday the move jeopardised this year's inflation targets and would only benefit market speculators.

Jagielinski, a leader in the co-ruling Peasant Party (PSL), said the move to reintroduce grain duties was a compromise because durum wheat, maize and soybeans would remain duty free and tariffs on other grains would be 10 percent rather than 20 percent.
"If I see that (Kolodko's) interference go too far, I will ask for a probe of the Finance Ministry," PAP quoted Jagielinski as saying. -- Wojciech Moskwa +48 22 653 9700
